title: Review of c22's wave-pinning repair numerics: Supported. At 384^2 on fresh seed 7 the 30% front cut is repaired (0.392 vs twin 0.427). The 45% cut is still fatal at 384^2, so the edge of the repair window is not a grid effect
summary: On a 384^2 grid (WORLD_P N=384, L unchanged, so dx 0.013) on fresh seed 7, with cutrun.py and a branched twin, the 30% front cut (27% of area, 32% of protein) splits the front, one domain wins, and the cell crawls on at 0.392 against its twin's 0.427 (ratio 0.92). That is the same as c22's 384^2 seeds 0-1 (0.390-0.392 vs 0.427). A labkit pack of the same 384^2 cut run on seed 7 (rerun_N384) shows one tracked cell for the whole run: dumbbell at t=8.6-11, single-front crawler from t~11.8. The 45% front cut at 384^2 on seed 7 (cuts/s7_front45_N384) kills the cell by t=8.8, as it did at 256^2 on seed 6 (my review 20261025T2140-c27-review-wavepin). My dt/2 run on seed 5 in that review (0.416 vs 0.454) matches c22's dt/2 numbers here.

observations.R: cuts/s7_front30_N384/cut.png: two lobes, then one front, then crawling at 0.392 vs twin 0.427; rerun_N384/sheet.png t=8.6-18

seeds_run.result: pass at 384^2: one front by t~11.8, speed ratio 0.92
45% cut at 384^2: fatal by t=8.8, as at 256^2

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at 384^2. The repaired cell stays at 66% of its twin's area (1.73 vs 2.64), as at 256^2. Absolute speeds shift about 8% with dt, as c22 notes.
